summary: zencleaner silently relays installer identity and license keys to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: zencleaner 1.0.0 ships a license-activation flow whose /api/license/activate and /api/license/deactivate endpoints — the required gate to use the advertised cleaner UI — POST the submitted license key, client IP, Windows COMPUTERNAME and USERNAME to a hardcoded Discord webhook (discord.com/api/webhooks/1555423493796012102/<token>) via urllib.request.urlopen in webhook_logger.py. The destination is not caller-configurable and the webhook URL is embedded verbatim in module-level source. The README states 'No telemetry, no data collection, no outbound calls', directly contradicting the behavior of the shipped code. The hardcoded webhook token is also a live credential that grants write access to the author's Discord channel to anyone who installs the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
